what_this_is: A frozen corpus of REPEATED events, used to measure the occurrence axis: repeat-event recall, occurrence-index exactness, and index stability across a re-measure.

provenance.source_of_the_moments: IMG_1822 (Apple 001 corpus), the first 48.0 s of the take, copied to a Ren-owned scratch file at 30 fps. The three moments are the occurrences the M0 baseline report adjudicated by eye on 30 fps frame strips: the device reaching the mouth at ~17-19 s, ~33.3-33.7 s and ~47 s.
provenance.adjudication: AGENT-ADJUDICATED, NOT HUMAN. The M0 baseline report records the occurrence-2 band as 33.30-33.70 s (+/- 6 frames) and says a human adjudicator must re-freeze it before the case is used as a scored benchmark. This corpus inherits that status: it measures the AXIS (which occurrence is named), not the frame accuracy of an onset.
provenance.why_five_fixtures_from_one_measurement: The axis is a function of (class, subject, source, time order). The five fixtures are the SAME three measured moments replayed under the five combinations the axis has to keep apart: one subject; a second subject; a second take; two classes; and one class spread over two takes. Nothing here is invented footage: every moment is a measured one.
provenance.not_a_benchmark_of_detection: These fixtures do NOT measure whether the engine FINDS the moments. That is the event lane's measurement (M7), which was licence-blocked on this machine when this corpus was frozen. The corpus starts from moments already measured.

fixtures.note: The M0 case as measured: one subject, one class, one source.
The same moments, counted for a DIFFERENT subject: the series is a class AND a subject.
The same moments in a SECOND source: the series is scoped to one source, so the numbering restarts there.
The same moments split across two classes: the class is part of the series, so the second class's first occurrence is the FIRST of that class.

One class, one subject, two sources: the second take's occurrences must not continue the first take's numbering, and an unscoped query must be refused rather than answered from whichever take came first.
